parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about special educational needs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have learned about special educational needs and include a
discussion about using children with special educational needs in psychological studies. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would use a questionnaire to find out about student attitudes towards
co-operative learning.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe co-operative learning, using examples.

text: A new teacher at your school uses the humanistic teaching strategy of co-operative learning and
you want to find out what students think about it.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would investigate which punishment strategy is most effective for modifying
the behaviour of a disruptive child.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the underlying theory on which these corrective strategies are based. 
Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Corrective strategies for disruptive behaviour include positive punishment (giving something
unpleasant) and negative punishment (removing something pleasant).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by a ‘self report questionnaire’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two studies that have used self report questionnaires to measure stress.

Answer this question.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have found out about health and safety and include a discussion

Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would use an interview to investigate which style of practitioner clothing is
preferred by patients.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the original study conducted by McKinstry and Wang or any alternative study on
practitioner non-verbal communication.

text: A study was conducted by McKinstry and Wang (1991) on patient preference for clothing style in
doctors. This study is now 25 years old and patient preference for doctors’ clothing style needs
reinvestigating.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would investigate which cognitive pain strategy is the most effective.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe how different cognitive strategies are used for managing pain. 
Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: There are a number of different cognitive strategies for managing pain. You want to find out which
is the most effective strategy.

parts.text:
Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘positive uses of sound (music) on consumer
behaviour’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study which has investigated the effect of music on consumer behaviour.

Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about environmental cognition.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have found out about environmental cognition and include a

Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you can test the effectiveness of Markus’s new evacuation message.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about evacuation plans.

text: Markus makes announcements at an outdoor sports venue where there are large crowds. He has
written an evacuation message to help people to leave safely in an emergency.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would conduct a field experiment to test the time it takes to vacate a parking
space when someone is waiting to park compared to when someone is not.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study showing how primary territory can be defended. 
Psychology and Abnormality
Section A
Answer this question.

text: A study by Ruback showed that when leaving a parking space, drivers would take longer when
another car was waiting to take the space, than when not. Ruback claimed this was due to people
defending parking space territory.

parts.text:

and compulsions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one way in which obsessions and compulsions have been measured.

Answer this question.

Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would treat his bus phobia using systematic desensitisation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe two other ways in which a phobia can be treated.

text: A man has not travelled on a bus for five years because of his phobia of public transport. You are
an expert in systematic desensitisation and can help him to travel on a bus.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would determine the effectiveness of a drug treatment for a mental disorder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe a model of abnormality which uses drug treatments. 
Psychology and Organisations
Section A
Answer this question.

text: A woman was admitted to a psychiatric hospital for assessment and treatment because she
wouldn’t get out of bed and refused to wash. The diagnosis was depression and she was prescribed
a drug. This drug did not work, so a different drug was prescribed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two extrinsic motivators.

parts.text: Suggest how you would conduct an experiment to determine the best decision-making model.

text: Your company is debating which of three decision-making models is best to select people for jobs.
You decide to conduct an experiment to see which of these models is the most effective.
